anthropic.summary: Anthropic separates two things. (1) Signing in to Anthropic's own unmodified Claude Code binary with your own Claude subscription is explicitly allowed, including when a platform hosts Claude Code, provided the platform follows the commercial conditions (binary unmodified, no removing auth methods, each end user signs in with their own credentials, no reselling or intermediating usage). (2) Third-party harnesses (OpenClaw and similar) that use subscription OAuth tokens directly are not covered by plan limits: since 2026-04-04 they draw from paid extra usage, and developers may not offer Claude.ai login in their own apps or route requests through plan credentials. The consumer Terms of Service themselves (effective Oct 8, 2025) were not changed in February 2026; the February change was to the Claude Code legal and compliance docs page.

anthropic.status_today: Two current Anthropic sources point in slightly different directions and neither is retracted. The support article (updated 2026-10-07) says Agent SDK, claude -p and 'third-party app usage' still draw from subscription limits, which reads as a relaxation since April. The legal page and login article still say developers may not offer Claude.ai login or route requests through plan credentials, and Anthropic may bill third-party tools from usage credits at its discretion. What is unambiguous today: an end user signing in to the unmodified Claude Code binary with their own subscription is allowed, including on a hosted computer. Whether third-party harnesses that use OAuth tokens directly are back on plan limits is NOT confirmed by any Anthropic statement found; 'OAuth is back' is supported only by OpenClaw's own docs and the paused-change support note.

google.summary: Since 2026-06-18 Gemini CLI no longer serves Google AI Pro, Ultra or free personal accounts; those moved to Antigravity CLI (agy). Google's terms say using third-party software to access Antigravity or Gemini CLI services (example: OpenClaw with OAuth) is a breach and may lead to suspension. The Antigravity FAQ also says wrapping agy inside third-party coding agents or applications is not supported under consumer plans. This is the most restrictive of the four vendors for a product that runs the official CLI.

timeline.event: Antigravity FAQ on headless agy in third-party apps.
timeline.quote: Antigravity CLI headless mode (agy -p) is intended for direct scripting and CI workflows. Wrapping agy inside third-party coding agents or applications, or automating account rotation, is not supported under consumer plans.
timeline.quote_note: spacing around the code span normalised

timeline.event: Antigravity CLI officially supports ACP so editors (Zed, JetBrains, Android Studio, Xcode) can launch agy acp as a subprocess using the user's cached sign-in.
timeline.quote: Your editor launches agy acp as a subprocess and talks to it with JSON-RPC over stdin and stdout.

timeline.event: Forum replies by user Ambati_Rajendra said running the unmodified agy binary from another tool is allowed, but consumer plans do not allow unattended background runs or task queues. This user has no Google flair on the forum, so this is NOT an official Google answer.
timeline.quote: Consumer plans ([FAQ]) don't allow unattended background runs, task queues, multi-agent "teammates," or credential sharing/rotation on oauth-personal.

google.sign_in: Gemini CLI today: Google account sign-in serves Gemini Code Assist Standard/Enterprise; individuals use an API key. Antigravity: personal Google accounts can sign in on any plan including free (antigravity.google/docs/faq).
google.ban_reversal: A secondary blog (metricnexus.ai) says Google reversed the February bans on 2026-02-27; not confirmed by any Google source read. Treat as unverified.
google.status_today: Restrictive and ambiguous for Madani. Running Google's official binary is not the same as OAuth token reuse, but the Antigravity FAQ explicitly says wrapping agy inside third-party applications is not supported on consumer plans, and unattended scheduled runs are the risky part. Official supported path for third-party agents: Google AI Studio or Vertex/Gemini Enterprise API keys.

xai.summary: Grok Build (xAI's CLI) signs in with your xAI/X account via browser on first launch, or uses XAI_API_KEY. xAI's own docs say Grok Build can be used headlessly in scripts or bots, or through ACP in other apps. No consumer-terms clause specific to third-party apps using a subscription was found.

timeline.event: Grok Build launched in early beta for SuperGrok and X Premium Plus subscribers.
timeline.quote: Available now to all SuperGrok and X Premium Plus subscribers. Install Grok Build with a single command and sign in with your account

timeline.event: Grok Build docs on sign-in and use in other apps.
timeline.quote: Grok Build is a powerful and extensible coding agent. Use it via an interactive TUI, headlessly in scripts or bots, or through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) in other apps.
timeline.also: On first launch, Grok opens a browser for authentication. In non-browser environments, use an API key

timeline.event: The X Subscription replaced standalone SuperGrok for new customers (Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100, Ultra $200).
timeline.quote: Today we're introducing The X Subscription, which brings together Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor, and X Premium in one plan.

timeline.event: Consumer terms last updated; they bar sharing account credentials but contain no clause found on third-party apps using a subscription.
timeline.quote: You may not share your account credentials or make your account available to anyone else, and are responsible for all activities that occur under your account.

xai.status_today: No restriction found on running the official Grok Build CLI with your own subscription; docs describe scripted and in-app (ACP) use. Absence of a clause is not a permission; no xAI statement addressing third-party desktop apps was found.
